content: 1. Clarithromycin and Telavancin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 2. Clarithromycin and Teniposide: Clarithromycin increases teniposide levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor. 3. Clarithromycin and Terbinafine: Clarithromycin increases terbinafine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 4. Clarithromycin and Tezacaftor: Clarithromycin increases tezacaftor levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust tezacaftor dosage if co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Monitor closely. 5. Clarithromycin and Thiamine: Clarithromycin decreases thiamine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use with caution and monitor. 6. Clarithromycin and Ticagrelor: Clarithromycin increases ticagrelor levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Monitor closely. 7. Clarithromycin and Tinidazole: Clarithromycin increases tinidazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 8. Clarithromycin and Tisotumab Vedotin: Clarithromycin increases tisotumab vedotin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to MMAE (active metabolite), raising the risk of adverse effects. Use with caution and monitor. 9. Clarithromycin and Tobramycin: Clarithromycin increases tobramycin levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor. 10. Omeprazole and Tofacitinib: Omeprazole increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. No specific dose adjustment is recommended unless co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 11. Clarithromycin and Tolvaptan: Clarithromycin increases tolvaptan levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor. 12. Clarithromycin and Tramadol: Clarithromycin increases tramadol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 13. Triclabendazole and Omeprazole: Triclabendazole increases omeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 14. Clarithromycin and Trimethoprim: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 15. Clarithromycin and Trimipramine: Clarithromycin increases trimipramine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 16. Triptorelin and Clarithromycin: Triptorelin increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use with caution and monitor. 17. Clarithromycin and Tropisetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 18. Clarithromycin and Ulipristal: Clarithromycin increases ulipristal levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 19. Clarithromycin and Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of these inhaled agents by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Clarithromycin and Upadacitinib: Clarithromycin increases upadacitinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 21. Clarithromycin and Valbenazine: Clarithromycin increases valbenazine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Clarithromycin and Valsartan: Clarithromycin increases valsartan levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1. Use with caution and monitor. 23. Clarithromycin and Vamorolone: Clarithromycin increases vamorolone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. Monitor closely. 24. Clarithromycin and Vardenafil: Clarithromycin increases vardenafil levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 25. Clarithromycin and Velpatasvir: Clarithromycin increases velpatasvir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 26. Clarithromycin and Venlafaxine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin and Verapamil: Clarithromycin increases verapamil levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased calcium channel blocker effects may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. Use with caution and monitor. 28. Clarithromycin and Vinblastine: Clarithromycin increases vinblastine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor. 29. Clarithromycin and Vincristine: Clarithromycin increases vincristine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor. 30. Clarithromycin and Vincristine Liposomal: Clarithromycin increases vincristine liposomal levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor. 31. Clarithromycin and Vinorelbine: Clarithromycin increases vinorelbine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 32. Omeprazole and Vismodegib: Omeprazole decreases vismodegib levels or effects by increasing gastric pH, which alters solubility and reduces bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Use with caution and monitor. 33. Clarithromycin and Zidovudine: Clarithromycin increases zidovudine toxicity through an unknown mechanism. Literature reports conflicting data. Separate administration by 2 to 4 hours. Use with caution and monitor. 34. Clarithromycin and Ziprasidone: Clarithromycin increases ziprasidone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 35. Clarithromycin and Zonisamide: Clarithromycin increases zonisamide levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor. 36. Clarithromycin and Zuranolone: Clarithromycin increases zuranolone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce zuranolone dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely.
